title: ICU pharmacology and drug infusions
summary: Practical ICU pharmacology: standard infusion dilutions and rate maths for vasoactive, sedative and other common infusions, dosing in obesity, AKI/CRRT and augmented renal clearance, liver dysfunction, QT-prolonging drugs and key interactions, and IV compatibility and line safety.

topics.title: Standard infusion dilutions and rate maths
topics.summary: Use one standard concentration per drug across the ICU, label the final concentration, and convert doses to mL/h with a single formula: rate (mL/h) = dose (mcg/kg/min) × weight (kg) × 60 ÷ concentration (mcg/mL). Double-check every high-alert infusion.

steps.title: Standardise
steps.detail: One concentration per drug per unit; prefilled or pharmacy-made syringes where possible; label drug, total amount, volume, final concentration, time and preparer.

steps.title: Weight-based per minute
steps.detail: mL/h = dose (mcg/kg/min) × kg × 60 ÷ mcg/mL. Example: noradrenaline 0.1 mcg/kg/min, 70 kg, 160 mcg/mL → 2.6 mL/h.

steps.title: Weight-based per hour
steps.detail: mL/h = dose (mg/kg/h) × kg ÷ mg/mL. Example: midazolam 0.05 mg/kg/h, 70 kg, 1 mg/mL → 3.5 mL/h.

steps.title: Fixed dose
steps.detail: mL/h = dose per hour ÷ concentration. Example: vasopressin 0.03 U/min = 1.8 U/h ÷ 0.4 U/mL = 4.5 mL/h.

steps.title: Independent double check
steps.detail: Second nurse/doctor verifies drug, concentration, pump programme and line for vasoactives, insulin, heparin, potassium, sedatives. Use pump drug libraries where available.

steps.title: Avoid gaps
steps.detail: 'Double-pump' or piggyback vasopressor syringe changes; never flush a vasopressor lumen.

doseCards.route: IV infusion (central preferred; peripheral short-term acceptable)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg at 0.1 mcg/kg/min with 160 mcg/mL = 2.6 mL/h.
20 U in 50 mL (0.4 U/mL): 0.03 U/min = 4.5 mL/h.
70 kg at 0.5 mcg/kg/h with 4 mcg/mL = 8.75 mL/h.

doseCards.verify: Check U-40 vs U-100 vial before drawing up.

mcg vs mg or per-minute vs per-hour errors produce 60-1000-fold overdoses.

pitfalls.text: Drawing U-40 insulin with a U-100 syringe (2.5-fold error).
Bolusing other drugs through the vasopressor lumen.
Mixing concentrations between shifts ('double strength' noradrenaline without relabelling).

pearls.text: Write orders in dose units (mcg/kg/min), not mL/h; let the chart convert.

nodes.text: Start via dedicated labelled line; document

consultantNotes.evidence: - Standard concentrations and smart pumps are patient-safety consensus recommendations to reduce infusion errors; Kanji 2010 shows how thin the compatibility evidence for shared lines is.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Many Indian ICUs still dilute per patient; adopting a unit-wide chart (laminated on each pump) is a cheap safety win.

topics.title: Drug dosing in obesity
topics.summary: Pick the dosing weight per drug: lipophilic loading doses and some antimicrobials by actual weight, most maintenance infusions and neuromuscular blockers by ideal or adjusted weight, and titrate sedatives to effect. Use therapeutic drug monitoring where available.

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: Record actual (total) body weight and height; estimate in bed with weighing scales or bed scales rather than guess.

steps.title: Weight scalars
steps.detail: IBW (Devine): men 50 + 0.91 × (height cm − 152.4); women 45.5 + 0.91 × (height cm − 152.4). Adjusted BW = IBW + 0.4 × (TBW − IBW).

steps.title: Titrate
steps.detail: Propofol, fentanyl and midazolam accumulate in adipose tissue with prolonged infusion; start on IBW/adjusted weight and titrate to RASS.

steps.title: Load generously
steps.detail: Hydrophilic drugs (beta-lactams, aminoglycosides) need full or higher loading doses; vancomycin load on actual weight (cap ~3 g) then TDM-guided; aminoglycosides on adjusted weight.

steps.title: Intubation
steps.detail: Suxamethonium 1-1.5 mg/kg actual weight; rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg on ideal (or lean) weight.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: UFH by actual weight with local cap and aPTT/anti-Xa; LMWH prophylaxis dose often increased when BMI ≥ 40 (local protocol, anti-Xa if available).

doseCards.dose: 20-35 mg/kg actual body weight, max ~3 g
doseCards.workedExample: 130 kg man: 25 mg/kg = 3250 mg → cap 3 g, infused over ≥ 3 h; then 15-20 mg/kg/dose guided by levels.
doseCards.verify: Loading range and cap differ between guidelines.

tables.title: Which weight? (common ICU drugs)
tables.caption: Conventions differ between sources; follow local protocol and monitor effect or levels.

redFlags.text: Delayed awakening after days of midazolam/fentanyl in a patient with BMI > 35: accumulation.

pitfalls.text: Dosing all sedative infusions on actual weight.
Under-loading antibiotics for fear of toxicity in sepsis.

pearls.text: Example: 170 cm man, 130 kg → IBW 66 kg, adjusted 91.6 kg.

nodes.text: Loading dose of hydrophilic antimicrobial or suxamethonium?
Use actual weight (with caps) then monitor levels

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: - Obesity increases volume of distribution for lipophilic drugs and raises lean mass, cardiac output and often renal clearance early; fat-laden liver may alter metabolism.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **Erstad & Barletta 2020:** review of sedative and analgesic dosing; little high-quality data, favours titration and lean/ideal scalars.
- **Pai 2000:** origin and limitations of IBW equations.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Asian body composition: higher fat percentage at lower BMI; WHO Asian cut-offs (overweight ≥ 23, obese ≥ 25 kg/m²) are used in India.

topics.title: Dosing in AKI, CRRT and augmented renal clearance
topics.summary: Never reduce loading doses for renal function. Adjust maintenance doses to measured or estimated clearance, recognising that creatinine is unreliable in unstable AKI, that CRRT removes many antibiotics, and that young septic or trauma patients often clear drugs faster than normal.

steps.title: Full dose
steps.detail: Loading dose depends on volume of distribution, not clearance – give the full dose in AKI and on RRT.

steps.title: Clearance
steps.detail: Cockcroft-Gault or measured 8-24 h urinary creatinine clearance; eGFR equations assume steady state and mislead in changing AKI.

steps.title: Don't under-dose
steps.detail: Many AKIs resolve within 48 h; for wide-therapeutic-index antibiotics (beta-lactams) delay renal down-adjustment for the first 24-48 h.

steps.title: Account for removal
steps.detail: Effluent 25 mL/kg/h gives roughly 25-35 mL/min of clearance for small, unbound drugs; dose accordingly and use TDM.

steps.title: Recognise
steps.detail: Measured CrCl > 130 mL/min (young, trauma, sepsis, TBI) leads to sub-therapeutic beta-lactam and vancomycin levels: higher or more frequent doses, prolonged infusions, TDM.

steps.title: Prolonged infusion
steps.detail: Meta-analysis: prolonged infusion lowered 90-day mortality; BLING III alone was not significant. Consider extended (3-4 h) or continuous infusion after a loading dose.

doseCards.dose: Full loading dose, then redose by levels (e.g. when level < 15-20 mg/L on intermittent HD; ~15 mg/kg every 24 h on CRRT as a starting point)

redFlags.text: Rising creatinine with nephrotoxin stacking (vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam, aminoglycoside, contrast, NSAID).

pitfalls.text: Halving a meropenem dose on day 1 of septic AKI because creatinine is 2.5.
Ignoring augmented clearance in a 25-year-old trauma patient.

pearls.text: Example CG: 70 y man, 60 kg, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL → (140 − 70) × 60 ÷ (72 × 1.2) ≈ 49 mL/min.

nodes.text: Adjust maintenance to estimated CrCl (delay 24-48 h in early sepsis AKI for wide-index drugs)

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **KDIGO 2011 update (Matzke):** framework for dosing in AKI and CKD.
- **Udy 2011:** ARC common in critically ill; sub-therapeutic levels.
- **BLING III 2024:** 7031 patients, continuous vs intermittent beta-lactam; 90-day mortality difference not significant.
- **Abdul-Aziz 2024 meta-analysis:** prolonged infusion associated with lower 90-day mortality.
consultantNotes.controversies: - CRRT antibiotic dosing tables vary widely; therapeutic drug monitoring is limited to vancomycin and aminoglycosides in most Indian ICUs.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Beta-lactam TDM is rarely available; extended infusions of meropenem (e.g. 1-2 g over 3 h every 8 h) are a pragmatic option.

topics.title: Dosing in liver dysfunction
topics.summary: No liver test predicts drug clearance well. In cirrhosis and acute liver failure prefer drugs with short half-lives or non-hepatic elimination, avoid long-acting sedatives, lower and titrate high-extraction and highly protein-bound drugs, and watch for encephalopathy and bleeding.

steps.title: Severity
steps.detail: Child-Pugh class guides labels (B: reduce, C: avoid or major reduction); MELD does not predict PK.

steps.title: Choose
steps.detail: Propofol or low-dose dexmedetomidine titrated; avoid midazolam and lorazepam infusions; fentanyl in small boluses rather than morphine (M6G accumulates in hepatorenal syndrome).

steps.title: Oral route
steps.detail: Oral bioavailability rises with portosystemic shunting (e.g. propranolol, morphine, midazolam) – reduce oral doses.

steps.title: Free fraction
steps.detail: Highly protein-bound drugs (phenytoin, valproate, ceftriaxone) have higher free levels; interpret total levels cautiously (use free phenytoin).

steps.title: Hepatotoxic and nephrotoxic
steps.detail: NSAIDs (renal failure, bleeding), aminoglycosides; paracetamol at 2-3 g/day is acceptable in cirrhosis.

redFlags.text: New confusion after sedative or opioid in cirrhosis: drug-precipitated encephalopathy.

pitfalls.text: Using midazolam infusions for agitation in hepatic encephalopathy.

pearls.text: Remifentanil (plasma esterases) and atracurium/cisatracurium (Hofmann) are organ-independent options.

nodes.text: Child-Pugh C or acute liver failure?
Start low, titrate, monitor sedation and levels
Reassess daily for encephalopathy and bleeding

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: - Clearance of high-extraction drugs depends on hepatic blood flow; low-extraction drugs on enzyme capacity and protein binding. Glucuronidation is relatively preserved compared with CYP oxidation.
consultantNotes.evidence: - **Verbeeck 2008:** review of PK changes and dose-adjustment principles in hepatic dysfunction.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Alcohol, viral hepatitis and NASH-related cirrhosis are common; many patients also take unregulated herbal remedies with hepatotoxic potential.

topics.title: QT prolongation, torsades and key ICU drug interactions
topics.summary: Stack-check QT drugs and risk factors (low K/Mg, bradycardia, female sex, structural heart disease). Stop offending drugs when QTc exceeds 500 ms or rises more than 60 ms, give IV magnesium for torsades, and watch the handful of interactions that cause real ICU harm.

steps.title: Baseline ECG
steps.detail: QTc before and after starting QT drugs; correct K to ≥ 4.0 mmol/L and Mg ≥ 2 mg/dL.

steps.title: Act
steps.detail: QTc > 500 ms or increase > 60 ms: stop or switch QT-prolonging drugs, continuous monitoring.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: Magnesium 2 g IV; unstable or pulseless: defibrillate; recurrent: overdrive pacing or isoprenaline to raise heart rate (if not congenital LQT).

steps.title: Check
steps.detail: Carbapenem + valproate (valproate levels collapse – seizures; avoid); linezolid + SSRIs/fentanyl/methylene blue (serotonin syndrome); fluconazole/voriconazole + midazolam, fentanyl, tacrolimus (CYP3A4 inhibition); rifampicin (induction); amiodarone + warfarin/digoxin (halve digoxin).

doseCards.dose: 2 g over 1-2 min if pulseless, otherwise over 10-15 min; repeat once or infuse 0.5-1 g/h
doseCards.workedExample: 2 g = 4 mL of 50% solution diluted to 20 mL.

redFlags.text: QTc > 500 ms with ventricular ectopy or pauses (short-long-short sequences).

pitfalls.text: Bazett over-corrects at high heart rates; use Fridericia when HR > 100.

pearls.text: Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia are the most fixable QT risks.

nodes.text: ECG (QTc), K and Mg; correct electrolytes

consultantNotes.evidence: - **AHA/ACCF 2010 (Drew):** recommendations for ECG monitoring and QT thresholds in hospital.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Azithromycin, levofloxacin, ondansetron and haloperidol are often co-prescribed; deliberate stack-checking at rounds avoids cumulative risk.

topics.title: IV compatibility, line management and extravasation
topics.summary: Give vasoactives through a dedicated labelled lumen, never Y-site unknown combinations, keep blood, parenteral nutrition and bicarbonate separate, and recognise extravasation early. Peripheral vasopressors are acceptable short-term with a good proximal vein, hourly checks and an extravasation plan.

steps.title: Dedicate
steps.detail: Vasopressors/inotropes on one lumen (no boluses); sedation/analgesia on another; PN and blood products separate; label every line at the hub.

steps.title: Compatibility
steps.detail: Use a compatibility chart before Y-siting; incompatible pairs include furosemide with midazolam or dobutamine, phenytoin with dextrose, pantoprazole with many drugs, ceftriaxone with calcium-containing fluids.

steps.title: Safe practice
steps.detail: Large vein proximal to wrist/antecubital fossa, ultrasound-guided if needed, hourly site checks, plan central access if > 24-48 h or rising dose.

steps.title: Act fast
steps.detail: Stop infusion, aspirate through cannula, elevate, infiltrate phentolamine 5-10 mg in 10 mL SC; mark area and photograph.

steps.title: Product specifics
steps.detail: Amiodarone and GTN in non-PVC or recommended sets; propofol sets changed every 12 h; insulin line primed to saturate binding.

doseCards.dose: 5-10 mg in 10 mL NS around the site within 12 h
doseCards.verify: Phentolamine supply in India is irregular; know your local alternative.

redFlags.text: Blanching, coolness or pain at a peripheral vasopressor site.

pitfalls.text: Flushing a vasopressor line to 'clear' it, giving the patient a bolus.

pearls.text: Cardenas-Garcia 2015: extravasation in 2% of 734 patients receiving peripheral vasoactives, none with tissue injury after phentolamine and nitroglycerin paste.

nodes.text: Stop infusion, aspirate, elevate; resite elsewhere
Local alternative (topical GTN/terbutaline per policy); surgical review if necrosis

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **Kanji 2010:** systematic review of 41 common ICU infusions (820 possible pairs): compatibility data exist for only 54% of pairs; 15% of studied pairs were incompatible and 9% had conflicting data.
- **Cardenas-Garcia 2015:** 734 patients, protocolised peripheral noradrenaline/dopamine/phenylephrine for 49 ± 22 h; extravasation in 2% with no tissue injury after phentolamine plus nitroglycerin paste; 13% eventually needed central access.
- **SSC 2026:** still suggests starting vasopressors peripherally rather than delaying for central access (conditional, very low certainty). Data are insufficient to set a safe duration, dose or cannula size; pooled complication rate ~6%. Use with caution where hourly site checks are not possible.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Triple-lumen CVCs are standard; where only two lumens are available, prioritise a dedicated vasopressor lumen.

options: Acceptable to start rather than delay
quiz.explanation: SSC 2026 suggests starting peripherally rather than delaying for central access: short term, through a good proximal vein, with hourly site checks.

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
drugs.indications: First-line vasopressor in septic and most vasodilatory shock.
drugs.adultDose: 0.05-0.5 mcg/kg/min (higher in refractory shock); start ~0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min titrated to MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.
drugs.preparationIndia: 2 mg/2 mL ampoules. Common syringe: 8 mg in 50 mL (160 mcg/mL) or 4 mg in 50 mL (80 mcg/mL) of NS or D5.
drugs.cautions: Extravasation necrosis; peripheral use acceptable short-term via a good proximal vein with monitoring. Digital/mesenteric ischaemia at high doses.
drugs.verify: Confirm salt vs base labelling of local ampoules.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine)
drugs.indications: Second vasopressor/inotrope in shock; anaphylaxis infusion.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1 mg/mL ampoules. Syringe: 4 mg in 50 mL (80 mcg/mL).

drugs.name: Vasopressin
drugs.indications: Add-on in septic shock when noradrenaline doses are escalating (commonly 0.25-0.5 mcg/kg/min; SSC 2026).
drugs.adultDose: 0.03 U/min fixed (up to 0.04 U/min); not weight-based.
drugs.preparationIndia: 20 U/mL 1 mL ampoules. Syringe: 20 U in 50 mL (0.4 U/mL); 0.03 U/min = 4.5 mL/h.
drugs.cautions: Digital, mesenteric and myocardial ischaemia; hyponatraemia. Terlipressin is a different drug (bolus doses in mg), and SSC 2026 suggests against it in septic shock.

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.indications: Low cardiac output with adequate MAP and filling.
drugs.preparationIndia: 250 mg vials/ampoules (volume varies by brand). Syringe: 250 mg in 50 mL (5000 mcg/mL).
drugs.cautions: Tachycardia, arrhythmia, hypotension from beta-2 vasodilatation.

drugs.name: Glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin)
drugs.indications: Hypertensive acute pulmonary oedema, ACS with ongoing pain or hypertension.
drugs.adultDose: 5-200 mcg/min titrated every 3-5 min (high-dose boluses used in SCAPE).
drugs.preparationIndia: 5 mg/mL ampoules (5 mL = 25 mg). Syringe: 50 mg in 50 mL (1 mg/mL = 1000 mcg/mL); 10 mcg/min = 0.6 mL/h.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension in RV infarct or preload dependence; avoid within 24-48 h of PDE-5 inhibitors; PVC adsorption (use non-PVC sets).

drugs.name: Midazolam
drugs.indications: Sedation when propofol/dexmedetomidine unsuitable; status epilepticus.
drugs.adultDose: Infusion 0.02-0.1 mg/kg/h (use lowest effective, daily interruption).
drugs.preparationIndia: 1 mg/mL (5 mL) and 5 mg/mL (1 mL, 10 mL) ampoules. Syringe: 50 mg in 50 mL (1 mg/mL).
drugs.cautions: Accumulates in obesity, AKI (active metabolite) and liver failure; CYP3A4 inhibitors (azoles, macrolides) prolong effect; delirium.

drugs.name: Fentanyl
drugs.adultDose: Infusion 0.5-2 mcg/kg/h (typical 25-150 mcg/h) dosed on ideal/adjusted weight in obesity.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50 mcg/mL in 2 mL and 10 mL ampoules. Syringe: 500 mcg in 50 mL (10 mcg/mL) or neat 50 mcg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Context-sensitive accumulation with prolonged infusion and obesity; chest wall rigidity with rapid bolus; CYP3A4 interactions; serotonin syndrome with linezolid/SSRIs.

drugs.name: Propofol
drugs.indications: Light sedation in ventilated patients; refractory status epilepticus.
drugs.adultDose: 5-50 mcg/kg/min (0.3-3 mg/kg/h); avoid > 4 mg/kg/h for > 48 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1% (10 mg/mL) 20 mL ampoules and 50 mL vials; run neat. 2% available.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension; propofol infusion syndrome (acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, arrhythmia, hypertriglyceridaemia); lipid calories 1.1 kcal/mL; change giving set every 12 h (6-12 h for open vials).

drugs.name: Dexmedetomidine
drugs.indications: Light sedation, agitation/delirium, facilitation of NIV and extubation.
drugs.adultDose: 0.2-1.4 mcg/kg/h; loading doses usually omitted in ICU because of bradycardia/hypotension.
drugs.preparationIndia: 100 mcg/mL ampoules (1 mL, 2 mL). Syringe: 200 mcg in 50 mL (4 mcg/mL).
drugs.cautions: Bradycardia, hypotension; does not provide deep sedation or amnesia.

drugs.name: Regular (soluble) insulin
drugs.adultDose: DKA 0.1 U/kg/h (or 0.14 U/kg/h without bolus); ICU glucose by protocol targeting 140-180 mg/dL.
drugs.preparationIndia: 40 U/mL (U-40) and 100 U/mL vials. Syringe: 50 U in 50 mL NS (1 U/mL).
drugs.cautions: U-40 vs U-100 confusion; adsorption to tubing (prime the line); hypokalaemia and hypoglycaemia.
drugs.verify: Check vial strength every time; use an insulin syringe matched to strength or measure in units only.

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin
drugs.indications: Therapeutic anticoagulation where rapid reversal or AKI precludes LMWH; CRRT circuits.
drugs.adultDose: VTE: 80 U/kg bolus then 18 U/kg/h (ACS: 60 U/kg max 4000 U, then 12 U/kg/h max 1000 U/h), adjusted to aPTT/anti-Xa.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5000 U/mL 5 mL vials (25,000 U). Syringe: 25,000 U in 50 mL (500 U/mL).
drugs.cautions: Use actual weight with a cap per local nomogram in obesity; HIT; bleeding.
drugs.verify: Obesity dosing caps vary by institutional nomogram.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.indications: AF with rapid ventricular response in haemodynamically fragile patients; VT; shock-refractory VF.
drugs.adultDose: 300 mg IV over 20-60 min, then 900 mg over 24 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 150 mg/3 mL ampoules. Dilute in 5% dextrose; infusions > 2 mg/mL via central line; use in-line filter per product.
drugs.cautions: Phlebitis peripherally; hypotension; QT prolongation (TdP uncommon); raises digoxin and warfarin effect.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate
drugs.indications: Torsades de pointes; hypomagnesaemia; QT-risk mitigation.
drugs.adultDose: TdP: 2 g IV over 1-2 min (pulseless) or 10-15 min; repeat or infuse 0.5-1 g/h.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension with rapid infusion; accumulates in AKI (monitor levels and reflexes).

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.indications: MRSA and other resistant Gram-positive infection.
drugs.adultDose: Loading 20-35 mg/kg actual body weight (max ~3 g), then 15-20 mg/kg every 8-12 h adjusted to AUC 400-600 or trough levels.
drugs.preparationIndia: 500 mg and 1 g vials; infuse ≤ 10 mg/min (1 g over ≥ 1 h).
drugs.cautions: Nephrotoxicity (especially with piperacillin-tazobactam), vancomycin infusion reaction with fast infusion.
drugs.verify: Loading ranges and caps vary between guidelines; follow local TDM protocol.

drugs.name: Phentolamine
drugs.indications: Extravasation of noradrenaline, adrenaline, dopamine or vasopressin.
drugs.adultDose: 5-10 mg diluted in 10 mL NS, infiltrated subcutaneously around the extravasation site within 12 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 10 mg/mL ampoules – supply is irregular in India; keep in the ICU or know the alternative (topical nitroglycerin, SC terbutaline) per local policy.
drugs.verify: Availability and alternatives depend on local formulary.

verify.reason: Standard dilutions listed are common Indian ICU practice and examples; every unit must use its own approved concentration chart, and labels must state the final concentration.
Indian noradrenaline ampoules are labelled variously as noradrenaline bitartrate or base equivalent; confirm whether doses are expressed as base (SSC convention) for your product.
U-40 (40 U/mL) and U-100 vials both circulate in India; confirm strength before preparing an infusion.
